title: Define publish contract and auto-refresh for multi-variant performance profiles
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: As we onboard larger models we publish multiple serving variants (fp16, int8, 4-bit quant, mixed-precision and sharded variants). Currently each variant gets a separate ad-hoc performance profile (latency/throughput/cost), which makes it hard for downstream teams to: 1) automatically select an appropriate fall-back at runtime, 2) reason about cost deltas between variants, and 3) keep published numbers fresh as kernels, quantization recipes, and runtime improvements land.

Goal: Define a canonical publish contract and automation that bundles multi-variant profiles into a single signed manifest per model-version. The manifest should: 1) enumerate variants with keys for architecture, quantization, sequence length anchor, and normalized cost/unit; 2) include provenance metadata (benchmark bundle id, platform/hardware, model checksum, profile generated_at); 3) expose time-to-live (TTL) and an auto-refresh policy that triggers sampled re-verification on infra/runtime changes; 4) produce a machine-verifiable signature so Console and runtime routing can trust the published data.

Scope: This ticket focuses on the product-facing contract (schema), ops automation triggers, and rollout plan. Implementation details for signing/key management will be coordinated with Security (follow-up ticket). Eng will produce serialization and publish APIs; Console will read and display manifests; Optimize will consume cost deltas for recommendations.

Out of scope: full KMS integration and enterprise attestation workflow (will be separate epics).

Success metrics: 
- 90% of newly onboarded model-versions publish a multi-variant manifest at publish time.
- Runtime fallbacks can select an alternate variant with a predictable latency/cost delta in 95% of routed fallback scenarios.
- Automated refresh jobs detect drift or infra-impacting merges and enqueue re-verification within 48 hours for affected manifests.
acceptance_criteria: Schema doc (Confluence): field-level descriptions, example manifest, and validation rules published
Signed manifest design reviewed and approved by Product, Eng, and Security (high-level approval sufficient)
Auto-refresh policy documented with trigger list (kernel updates, quant-recipe changes, regional perf regressions, infra rolling updates)
Console shows manifest in model detail page with variant comparison and cost-normalized numbers
Runtime routing can fetch manifest and map fallback rules (mapping test harnesses in ENG)
